Both actions are complete. Here's a summary of what I did:

1. **Investigated**: `checkout-api` was running v2.3.1, which was unhealthy in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an elevated error rate of 0.18. Deployment history confirmed v2.3.1 was the only unhealthy production release; the most recent healthy production release was **v2.3.0**.

2. **Rolled back**: Successfully rolled `checkout-api` back to **v2.3.0** in all production regions. The service is now healthy (error rate 0.002).

3. **Opened incident**: Created SEV2 incident **INC-0002** ("checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy"), which paged the on-call engineer, documenting the failure and the rollback to v2.3.0. (The first attempt timed out, so I retried and it succeeded.)

Note: I did not deploy any new version, so no change-manager approval was required — the rollback restored a previously healthy production release.
